Source [S2] states that 'Different interpolation functions require different amounts of computation because they have different spatial extents,' directly linking computational complexity and spatial extent (number of neighbors) to the choice of kernel. Regarding frequency response, Source [S2] explains that the nearest-neighbor kernel (rect function) is a 'poor low-pass filter' because its frequency domain characteristics (sinc function) allow 'stopband energy to get through,' causing aliasing. Conversely, higher-order methods like cubic are associated with 'publication-quality imagery' and fewer artifacts, implying a trade-off towards blurring or smoother frequency response at the cost of higher computation. Source [S1] corroborates the computational cost and quality differences (artifacts vs. quality) associated with different kernels.
